title: There are no maps between bounded above complexes over a regular ring when their support ranges are separated by the dimension

standard_prerequisites.name: A bounded above complex may be replaced by its truncation above the vanishing bound in low degrees without changing the Ext groups in question
standard_prerequisites.use: Puts the representing complex in the normal form in which the top degree argument applies.

standard_prerequisites.name: A short exact sequence of complexes with the shift of a term in the middle gives a distinguished triangle, so the vanishing statement can be checked on the two outer pieces
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement by induction on the number of nonzero terms to the case of a single module placed in one degree.

standard_prerequisites.name: Over a regular ring of finite dimension every module has a projective resolution of length at most the dimension, and a map of complexes from a bounded complex of projectives concentrated in a range to a complex vanishing above a lower bound is zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the final vanishing, which is exactly the statement for the single module case.

core_obligations: Replace the representing bounded above complex by its truncation above the given vanishing bound so that it vanishes in degrees at most k, and record that this does not change the problem (proof lines 20774-20778).

Use the distinguished triangle of the top term and the truncation below it to reduce by induction on the top degree n to the case where the complex is a single module placed in degree m for some m greater than k (proof lines 20778-20784).

In that case, use that the regular ring has finite global dimension d to produce a projective resolution of the module of length at most d, and view it as a bounded complex of projectives concentrated in the degrees from m - d to m representing the module in degree m (proof lines 20784-20791).

Choose a representative of the second object vanishing above degree k - d, so that no nonzero map of complexes can exist between the two representatives because their supports are disjoint, and conclude the vanishing of the Hom group in the derived category (proof lines 20791-20796).
proof_roadmap: Normalize the first representative by truncation and reduce by induction to a single module placed in one degree (proof lines 20774-20784).
Resolve that module by projectives of length at most the dimension of the regular ring (proof lines 20784-20791).
Compare supports: no map of complexes exists between the two chosen representatives, which gives the vanishing (proof lines 20791-20796).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that over a Noetherian regular ring of finite dimension d there are no maps in the derived category between a bounded above complex vanishing in degrees at most k and a bounded above complex vanishing in degrees at least k minus d plus one (statement lines 20766-20772). The proof normalizes the first complex, reduces by a double induction on the top degree to the case of a single module placed in one degree, resolves that module by projectives of length at most d using finite global dimension, and then observes that the two representatives have disjoint supports so that no map of complexes between them exists (proof lines 20774-20796). The separation of the support ranges by exactly the dimension is what makes the final comparison of supports work.
